entries.source: Lakkaraju et al. 2017, The Selective Labels Problem, KDD, DOI 10.1145/3097983.3098066
entries.concept_borrowed: Observed outcomes can depend on historical human selection, making unselected cases systematically unlabeled or differently observed.
entries.use: Treat post-selection scholarly outcomes as selection-affected and prohibit causal interpretation as intrinsic value without additional identification.
entries.difference: Our setting is scientific-attention allocation, not judicial decisions; the identification problem is inherited, not novel.

entries.source: Settles 2009, Active Learning Literature Survey, UW-Madison TR1648
entries.concept_borrowed: Allocate scarce oracle labels among abundant unlabeled candidates; uncertainty and diversity are established query strategies.
entries.use: Baseline uncertainty/exploration policies and novelty challenge.
entries.difference: Our target is realised downstream epistemic value under scientific selection, not classifier label efficiency.
entries.supports: Human evaluation scarcity and uncertainty allocation are established prior art.

entries.source: Uzzi et al. 2013, Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact, Science, DOI 10.1126/science.1240474
entries.concept_borrowed: Atypical combinations as one operationalisation of scientific novelty.
entries.use: Candidate novelty measure only as a sensitivity analysis.
entries.difference: Not treated as ground truth novelty.
entries.supports: Atypical combinations can associate with impact.

entries.source: Fontana et al. 2020, New and atypical combinations, Research Policy, DOI 10.1016/j.respol.2020.104063
entries.concept_borrowed: Novelty indicators are construct-sensitive and may overlap interdisciplinarity.
entries.use: Requires independent validation and multiple novelty measures.
entries.difference: Used primarily as a falsification constraint.
entries.supports: Do not collapse novelty to a single embedding/combinatorial score.

entries.source: Teplitskiy et al. 2022, Is novel research worth doing?, PNAS, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2118046119
entries.concept_borrowed: Direct empirical test of novelty and peer-review acceptance across journals.
entries.use: Counterevidence to any prior assumption that peer review systematically suppresses novelty.
entries.difference: Our programme tests allocation policies under varying attention pressure rather than estimating existing peer-review novelty preference.
entries.supports: Novel manuscripts were not systematically disfavoured in their studied journal samples.

entries.concept_borrowed: API1/API2 coexist and older conferences can require legacy schemas.
entries.use: Acquisition must preserve raw responses and year-specific invitation provenance.
entries.difference: Engineering dependency, not a research contribution.

entries.source: Qi et al. 2013, Rule-based deduplication of article records from bibliographic databases, Database, DOI 10.1093/database/bat086
entries.concept_borrowed: Bibliographic entity resolution should combine title, author and identifier evidence and may use approximate string matching rather than a single field.
entries.use: Track A resubmission/lineage audit uses exact normalized title plus author overlap as the primary high-specificity rule and treats approximate title matching as sensitivity only.
entries.difference: We retain later manuscript records as lineage evidence rather than collapsing duplicate database records.
entries.supports: Conservative title+author lineage detection and explicit false-positive control.

entries.source: Rathbone et al. 2015, Better duplicate detection for systematic reviewers, Systematic Reviews, DOI 10.1186/2046-4053-4-6
entries.concept_borrowed: Combining title and author evidence with fuzzy name/string handling can improve duplicate-record sensitivity while preserving specificity.
entries.use: Supports a separately reported near-title lineage sensitivity stratum rather than broad semantic matching.
entries.difference: Our target is manuscript evolution across conference years, not duplicate citations in one review corpus.

entries.source: ASySD 2023, Automated Systematic Search Deduplicator, PMCID PMC10483700
entries.concept_borrowed: Bibliographic deduplication can use staged blocking criteria followed by stronger field-similarity checks.
entries.use: Track A blocks on title similarity and then requires author-surname overlap before admitting sensitivity lineage edges.
entries.difference: No records are deleted or automatically merged; lineage flags narrow interpretation of later outcomes.
entries.supports: Staged blocking and conservative candidate linkage.

entries.source: Codreanu et al. 2026, AI in Science: Early Insights, Google / Google DeepMind / MIT FutureTech
entries.concept_borrowed: Early survey and usage evidence that AI-assisted science may shift bottlenecks downstream, increase untested-hypothesis backlogs, create verification demand, and tilt researchers toward safer incremental questions.
entries.use: Treat as external empirical motivation for scarcity-migration and validation-cost-distortion hypotheses; preserve the report's selection-bias, disciplinary-heterogeneity and non-causal limitations.
entries.difference: The report documents early associations and perceptions; the Agalmic programme would need to identify allocation effects under controlled or prospectively measured resource constraints.
entries.supports: The generic downstream-bottleneck claim is empirically plausible but not sufficient as an Agalmic novelty claim.

entries.source: Hao et al. 2026, Artificial intelligence tools expand scientists’ impact but contract science’s focus, Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09922-y
entries.concept_borrowed: AI-augmented research is associated with greater individual scientific output and impact while collective topic coverage contracts and activity moves toward data-rich areas.
entries.use: Use as triangulation for a possible tractability or validation-cost selection effect, without treating the observational association as causal proof.
entries.difference: The Agalmic target is the allocation mechanism linking resource pressure to candidate survival, not the descriptive topic-contraction result itself.
entries.supports: Potential collective selection effects can coexist with individual productivity gains.

entries.source: Rana, Varshney & Varshney 2026, AI-driven Acceleration and the Evaluation Bottleneck in Science: A Conceptual Framework, DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7318643
entries.concept_borrowed: AI can expand scientific generative capacity faster than institutional capacity to evaluate, verify and contest claims, creating an evaluation bottleneck.
entries.use: Set the novelty boundary explicitly: Agalmic Research must not claim originality for the broad AI-evaluation-bottleneck thesis.
entries.difference: Agalmic Research focuses on whether heterogeneous downstream scarcity changes allocation and realised epistemic value, especially for expensive-to-validate candidates.
entries.supports: The evaluation-bottleneck concept is occupied prior art; contribution must be narrower and empirical.
